Hi Ross,

Weird that this doesn't work for you. I have no problems with my very similar setup.

I have:

require('tuneR')
setWavPlayer("play")  # the SoX play command

Here's a stab at it: I wonder if you might have multiple versions of .RProfile? E.g. if you have an RProfile in your home directory as well as one in the directory where you're invoking R, I'm not sure what the behavior is. You might try adding something like

print("I have set the wav player")

at the end of your file to make sure you're editing the right file.

best,
jesse

system("sox -V tico.wav /Users/rossahmed/Desktop/out.wav bandreject 4000, 2000)

messages.subject: Amplitude scale and strange oscillo() plots
messages.subject_clean: Amplitude scale and strange oscillo() plots
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I've just discovered seewave today. I'm a phonetics student trying to find cleaner looking plots for spectrograms/waveforms than what Praat offers. I really like the oscillo() function except it's acting quite strange. The first question is, I'm not quite sure how to specify dB labels on the y-axis - can someone clarify this for me?

The second question is the strange-acting part. When I call oscillo(ake,from=0.82,to=.84), nothing happens in the plot window. I have to call it twice before the plot does anything. If I call it again, the plot window goes blank and only after a 2nd call, does anything show. But the first and third time I call it (as well as the 2nd and 4th "working" times) there's the strange looking squished plot on the sideline (image attached).

I'm running R 3.0.2 with RStudio 0.98.484 on Mavericks 10.9.1.

Thanks!
Nay

> Hi all,
>
> I've just discovered seewave today. I'm a phonetics student trying to find cleaner looking plots for spectrograms/waveforms than what Praat offers. I really like the oscillo() function except it's acting quite strange. The first question is, I'm not quite sure how to specify dB labels on the y-axis - can someone clarify this for me?

The y axis of the oscillo refers to a relative scale "normalised" between -1 and 1, withtout unit. Oscillogram are very rarely ploted on a dB scale (relative or absolute).

>
> The second question is the strange-acting part. When I call oscillo(ake,from=0.82,to=.84), nothing happens in the plot window. I have to call it twice before the plot does anything. If I call it again, the plot window goes blank and only after a 2nd call, does anything show. But the first and third time I call it (as well as the 2nd and 4th "working" times) there's the strange looking squished plot on the sideline (image attached).
>

This is because you probably plotted a spectrogram before and I could not find a nice way to clean up the layout of the graphical window after a spectrogram plot. You need to close the window (dev.off()).
Jerome

messages.subject: RE: [seewave] Cut tico into 4 wave files using sox
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] Cut tico into 4 wave files using sox
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ross,

As far as I know, the only way to do this with sox would be to use seewave to figure out the times at which you wish to cut your file (in the manner that Jesse suggested), and then use a call to sox to actually do the cutting. You might consider using the afilter() in seewave to remove all amplitudes below a threshold. Then you could look for the start/stop times of anything louder than that with env().

However, if you're willing to fool around with sox a bit more, you could check out the "silence" effect in sox. This effect allows you to trim "silence" at what ever threshold you want (so it doesn't actually have to be silence) before a note, and then after.  So you can tell sox to trim the silence before you reach a given threshold, and then trim everything after after a given silence threshold has been reached. That would get you the first note.  Then you would have to call silence again (I think) and ask it to skip over the first note and get the second, etc. This could work if you know how many notes you're expecting, but it would probably be more trouble than it's worth if you're extracting many or an unknown number of notes.

I find the silence effect a bit difficult to figure out, but there's a great explanation of it here (http://digitalcardboard.com/blog/2009/08/25/the-sox-of-silence/) if you're interested.

Steffi

messages.subject: RE: [seewave] Cut tico into 4 wave files using sox
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] Cut tico into 4 wave files using sox
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

The function timer() should do the job, but be aware that finding the
start and end of a signal might be tricky. tico has a very good SNR.

##########
data(tico)
res <- timer(tico, f=22050, threshold=5, msmooth=c(50,0))

for(i in 1:length(res$s.start))
{
   note <- cutw(tico, from = res$s.start[i], to = res$s.en[i], out="Wave")
   writeWave(note, filename=paste("note-", i, ".wav", sep=""))
}
##########

Best,

Jerome
